title: Emergency Contraception (ECP): Reducing Unintended Pregnancies
brief_summary: Emergency contraception is a method of birth control that can be used up to three days after sexual intercourse. Emergency contraceptive pills (ECPs) can be given to a woman before she needs them (advance provision) or when she needs them (emergency provision). This study will compare these two methods of providing ECPs.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Patient at a participating clinic

Exclusion Criteria

* Pregnant
* Medical or surgical procedure preventing pregnancy (e.g., tubal ligation, hysterectomy)
* Norplant or IUDs
* Desires to become pregnant
